row.title: Alspach's decomposition conjecture for abelian Cayley graphs
row.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group with a symmetric generating set $S$. The Cayley graph

$$
\mathop{\mathsf{Cay}}(G;S)
$$

has no loops.

**Alspach's conjecture.** The Cayley graph $\mathop{\mathsf{Cay}}(G;S)$ can be decomposed into hamiltonian cycles, together with a $1$-factor if its valency is odd.

This conjecture extends the known decomposition of Cartesian products of undirected cycles into edge-disjoint hamiltonian cycles. The supplied text states the conjecture but does not indicate that it has been resolved in the stated generality.
row.source_name: Iren Darijani, Babak Miraftab and Dave Witte Morris, “Arc-disjoint hamiltonian paths in Cartesian products of directed cycles”, arXiv:2203.11017 (2022).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11017

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2022).

row.title: The conjecture that every triangle-free planar graph is POSH
row.statement: A planar graph is **POSH** (partial one-sided Hamiltonian) if it is a spanning subgraph of a graph admitting a plane embedding with a one-sided Hamiltonian cycle. **Triangle-free planar graph conjecture.** Every triangle-free planar graph is POSH. The conjecture would establish POSH for a broad sparse class of planar graphs and is presented as a possible generalization of the paper's bipartite-graph result; its resolution is not specified in the source.

row.title: The greedy Tamari interval–constellation bijection conjecture
row.statement: Let $m$ be a positive integer. Consider greedy $m$-Tamari intervals whose maximal element has $n_i$ ascents of length $i$ for each $i\ge 1$, including a first ascent of length $\ell$. Consider $(m+1)$-constellations with $n_i$ white faces of degree $(m+1)i$ for each $i\ge 1$, including a white root face of degree $(m+1)\ell$. **The greedy Tamari interval–constellation conjecture.** The number of such greedy $m$-Tamari intervals equals the number of such $(m+1)$-constellations. This conjecture seeks a bijective explanation of the enumerative equality proved earlier in the paper; finding such a bijection remains open.
row.source_name: Mireille Bousquet-Mélou and Frédéric Chapoton, “Intervals in the greedy Tamari posets”, arXiv:2303.18077 (2023).
row.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2023).

row.title: Zanello's unimodality strengthening of Bergeron's Gaussian inequality
row.statement:
Let $a,b,c,d$ be positive integers satisfying

$$
0<a\leq b<c\leq d,\qquad ad=bc.
$$

Consider the symmetric Gaussian-polynomial difference

$$
\binom{b+c}{b}_q-\binom{a+d}{a}_q.
$$

**Zanello's conjecture.** Its coefficients are non-negative and unimodal. The source describes this as a strengthening of the preceding Gaussian inequality and notes that Zanello treated the special case $a\leq3$; the general assertion remains open in the supplied text.
row.source_name: Tewodros Amdeberhan and David Callan, “Gaussian inequality”, arXiv:2304.03395 (2023).

row.title: Categorical graph minor conjecture
row.statement: Let $cmathcal{GM}$ be the category of graphs and minor morphisms. A category is **Noetherian over a ring** if its associated module categories satisfy the relevant ascending-chain finiteness property. **Categorical graph minor conjecture.** The category $cmathcal{GM}$ is Noetherian over any Noetherian ring. This is a categorical strengthening of the Robertson–Seymour graph minor theorem. The paper states that, together with the categorical Robertson conjecture, it would imply universal finite generation for homology of graph configuration spaces.

row.title: Accessibility conjecture for quasi-transitive graphs quasi-isometric to minor-excluded graphs
row.statement: A graph $\Gamma$ is **minor-excluded** if some finite graph is not a minor of $\Gamma$. A graph is **accessible** if it admits a finite decomposition over finite separators with pieces having at most one end. **Accessibility conjecture for minor-excluded quasi-isometry classes.** Let $\Gamma$ be a connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive graph, and suppose $\Gamma$ is quasi-isometric to a minor-excluded graph. Then $\Gamma$ is accessible. This is motivated by the known accessibility of connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive minor-excluded graphs and remains open under the stated quasi-isometry hypothesis.

row.title: The augmenting-path meta-conjecture for infinite structures
row.statement: Consider theorems about finite combinatorial structures that admit proofs by augmenting paths. **Augmenting-path meta-conjecture.** Such theorems should remain true in a structural form for infinite structures, possibly under some restrictions. This principle is motivated by infinite structural generalizations of finite results including Menger's theorem, the Ford–Fulkerson theorem, Tutte's matching theorem, Edmonds' matroid intersection theorem, and the Lovász–Cherkassky theorem. The source describes it as a somewhat vague meta-conjecture and gives no general proof or resolution.

row.title: Harary and Lauri's class reconstruction conjecture for trees
row.statement:
Let $T$ be a finite tree, and let $\operatorname{crn}(T)$ denote its class reconstruction number. For the class of trees, write $\operatorname{crn}(\mathcal{T})=\max_T\{\operatorname{crn}(T)\}$, where $\mathcal{T}$ is the class of finite trees. **Harary and Lauri's conjecture.** The class reconstruction number of the class of trees is 2:

$$
\operatorname{crn}(\mathcal{T})=2.
$$

Harary and Lauri had shown that the class reconstruction number is at most 3; the conjecture asserts that the upper bound can be improved to 2. The supplied text gives no evidence that this conjecture has been resolved.
row.source_name: Ilia Krasikov, Yehuda Roditty and Bhalchandra D. Thatte, “On the class reconstruction number of trees”, arXiv:2312.17026 (2024).
row.references:

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2023). “This conjecture was proved by Myrvold .”

row.title: Strong Lovász conjecture for finite connected vertex-transitive graphs
row.statement: Let $G$ be a finite connected vertex-transitive graph. A graph is **Hamilton connected** if it has a Hamilton path between any two vertices, and **Hamilton laceable** if it is bipartite and has a Hamilton path between any two vertices from different bipartition classes. **Strong Lovász conjecture.** The graph $G$ is Hamilton connected, Hamilton laceable, a cycle, or one of the five known counterexamples. This strengthens Lovász's conjecture on Hamiltonicity in vertex-transitive graphs and encompasses questions about Hamilton-connected and Hamilton-laceable vertex-transitive graphs. The five exceptional counterexamples are not identified in the supplied text.

row.title: The $K_6$ minor conjecture for triangles and induced $K_{3,3}$ minors
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A **minor** of $G$ is obtained by deleting vertices and edges and contracting edges; an **induced minor** is obtained by deleting vertices and edges and contracting connected vertex sets. A **triangle** is a cycle of length three.

**$K_6$ minor conjecture.** If $G$ contains $K_6$ as a minor, then $G$ contains a triangle as a subgraph or $G$ contains $K_{3,3}$ as an induced minor.

This proposes a structural consequence of having a $K_6$ minor, separating the presence of a triangle from the induced-minor obstruction $K_{3,3}$. The source presents it as an open proposal and gives no resolution.

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

row.title: Dejter's four-operation conjecture for efficient total colorings of cubic graphs
row.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite connected simple cubic graph of girth $4$. An **efficient total coloring** (ETC) is a total coloring in which each color class induces an efficient dominating set on the vertex set. The cube $Q_3$ is the 3-dimensional cube graph.

**Dejter's four-operation conjecture.** Every ETC of $\Gamma$ is obtained via the iterative genus-increasing procedure of Corollary~, departing from $Q_3$, through four constructive operations: periodic extensions, accordion unfoldings, cycle exchanges, and ETCings.

The conjecture proposes a complete construction of efficient total colorings for finite connected simple cubic graphs of girth $4$. The source gives the construction framework but no resolution of the claim.

row.title: The Local Irregularity Conjecture excluding the bow-tie graph
row.statement:
Let $B$ be the bow-tie graph, and let $G$ be a connected graph that is locally irregularly colorable. Write $\operatorname{lir}(G)$ for its locally irregular chromatic index.

**Local Irregularity Conjecture.** If $G\neq B$, then

$$
\operatorname{lir}(G)\leq 3.
$$

This is the improved form of the original conjecture after the bow-tie graph was found to require four colors. The source reports this as a conjecture established by Sedlar and Škrekovski, with the bound proved for cacti other than $B$.
row.source_name: Igor Grzelec, Tomáš Madaras, Alfréd Onderko and Roman Soták, “On a new problem about the local irregularity of graphs”, arXiv:2405.13893 (2024).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13893

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2024).

row.title: Plummer–Stiebitz–Toft reformulation for independence number two
row.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph with independence number $\alpha(G)$. Let $K_r$ denote the complete graph on $r$ vertices.

**Plummer–Stiebitz–Toft conjecture.** Every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)\leq2$ contains $K_{\lceil n/2\rceil}$ as a minor.

The paper states this as a reformulation of Hadwiger's conjecture for graphs with independence number at most two. A general proof is not known; the paper records a weaker $K_{\lceil n/3\rceil}$ minor result as evidence for it.

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

row.title: Quasi $n$-bottlenecking conjecture
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, say that $G$ is **coarsely $n$-bottlenecked** when it satisfies the coarse $n$-bottlenecking condition, and say that a graph is **$n$-edge bottlenecked** when it satisfies the corresponding discrete condition.

**Quasi $n$-bottlenecking conjecture.** If $G$ is coarsely $n$-bottlenecked, then it is quasi-isometric to an $n$-edge bottlenecked graph.

This conjecture seeks a quasi-isometric discrete model for coarsely $n$-bottlenecked graphs. The supplied text presents it as a proposed conjecture, and gives no resolution.

row.title: Characterization of connected graphs whose geodesic metric satisfies the Menger condition
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a nonempty connected graph. Write $V(G)$ for its vertex set and $d_G$ for its geodesic distance. Let $\mathfrak{MB}$ denote the class of metric spaces $(X,d)$ such that

$$
d(x,z)=d(x,y)+d(y,z)
$$

whenever $d(x,z)\geqslant\max\{d(x,y),d(y,z)\}$. **The graph characterization conjecture.** The metric space $(V(G),d_G)$ belongs to $\mathfrak{MB}$ if and only if one of the following holds: $G$ is isomorphic to a path; $G$ is isomorphic to the cycle $C_4$; $G$ is isomorphic to a ray $R$; or $G$ is isomorphic to a double ray $DR$. row.title: Aldred–Funk–Jackson–Labbate–Sheehan conjecture on 2-factor isomorphic graphs
row.statement: Let $G$ be a connected $k$-regular bipartite graph. A graph is **2-factor isomorphic** when all its $2$-factors are isomorphic, and it is **2-factor Hamiltonian** when every $2$-factor is a Hamiltonian circuit. **Aldred–Funk–Jackson–Labbate–Sheehan's conjecture.** The graph $G$ is $2$-factor isomorphic if and only if it is $2$-factor Hamiltonian. The survey notes that this unrestricted form is false, through a construction of non-Hamiltonian connected $2$-factor isomorphic cubic bipartite graphs.
row.source_name: D. Labbate and F. Romaniello, “An updated survey on 2-Factors of Regular Graphs”, arXiv:2408.04642 (2024).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.04642

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of August 2024); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

row.title: Po's general LSM constraint conjecture for crystallographic lattices
row.statement: Let a crystallographic group $G$ act on a lattice, and let a **symmetric short-range-entangled phase** (sym-SRE phase) mean a phase preserving the symmetry and having no intrinsic long-range entanglement. The lattice may be smoothly deformed by lattice homotopy, which preserves its anomaly, and a **trivial lattice** is one smoothly deformable to a configuration with no obstruction to a sym-SRE phase. **Po's general LSM constraint conjecture.** A sym-SRE phase is possible only when the lattice is smoothly deformable to a trivial lattice. This conjecture generalizes Lieb–Schultz–Mattis-type anomaly constraints to general crystallographic groups; the source presents it as a conjectural criterion for when symmetric short-range-entangled phases can occur.
row.source_name: Chunxiao Liu and Weicheng Ye, “Crystallography, Group Cohomology, and Lieb-Schultz-Mattis Constraints”, arXiv:2410.03607 (2026).

row.title: The Hamiltonian decomposition conjecture for regular graphs
row.statement: Let $G$ be an $N$-regular graph on $n$ vertices. A **Hamiltonian cycle** is a cycle that meets every vertex, and a **perfect matching** is a matching covering every vertex. **The Hamiltonian decomposition conjecture.** If $N\geq \left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor$, then $G$ has a decomposition into Hamiltonian cycles and at most one perfect matching. The conjecture predicts a Hamiltonian decomposition at the natural degree threshold; the source presents it as a related conjecture and gives no resolution.

row.title: The perfect 1-factorization conjecture for complete graphs
row.statement: Let $K_{2n}$ be the complete graph on $2n$ vertices. A **1-factorization** is a decomposition of its edges into perfect matchings, and it is perfect when the union of any two distinct 1-factors is a Hamiltonian cycle. **The perfect 1-factorization conjecture.** Every complete graph $K_{2n}$ with an even number of vertices admits a perfect 1-factorization. The conjecture is a strengthening of ordinary 1-factorization for complete graphs; the source attributes it to `Ko` and does not state whether it has been resolved.

row.title: Strong Erdős–Hajnal property for the directed triangle
row.statement:
Let the directed triangle mean the cyclic tournament on three vertices, and say that a tournament has the Strong Erdős–Hajnal property when it satisfies the strong Erdős–Hajnal conjecture. **Directed-triangle conjecture.** The directed triangle has the Strong Erdős–Hajnal property.

This is presented as a special case of the strong Erdős–Hajnal conjecture. The supplied text does not state whether this special case has been resolved.
